Status: SQLite and PostgreSQL measured locally; SQL Server unmeasured. Experimental only.
Units: milliseconds except counts, bytes and operations/second
Statistics: Warm-ups excluded. Median, observed range and nearest-rank P95. Burst requests are correlated; one wall interval per burst.

Fixture.Generator: DatabaseFixture.ps1, identical arithmetic fields/JSON to SQLite

Boundaries.Endpoint: HTTP response plus JSON-to-object parsing; pooled database connection in handler
Boundaries.Import: Whole script locally, or submit + 50ms completion polling + pipeline retrieval; fixture decoding and batch JSON preparation included
Boundaries.Burst: One earliest-worker-start to latest-worker-end wall interval, including between-operation driver work
Boundaries.Direct: Native Measure-Command around helper call/return, SQL, object construction and owned-connection disposal; serialization and checks follow clock

Server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 on x86_64-windows, compiled by msvc-19.44.35229, 64-bit

Metadata.Connection: TCP 127.0.0.1:5432; SCRAM password; SSL disabled in benchmark; no remote host

Evidence.Preservation: Three measured database custom dumps and SQL schemas; operational dump restored and field-checked; archive is independent of installed server

Limitations: Same workstation/storage but later, unpaired provider passes; no universal ranking or isolated engine timings.
Warm synthetic tables of at most 10,000 records; ASCII x payloads compress unusually well with PostgreSQL TOAST. No production size or capacity estimate.
PostgreSQL JSONB normalization differs from SQLite JSON text. Expression B-tree indexes, not GIN; scan phase removes only the expression index and runs separately.
Direct outer clocks use native Measure-Command; SQLite used an explicit Stopwatch. Serialization is outside direct read clocks. No measured subtraction of harness overhead.
PostgreSQL defaults include 128 MiB shared buffers plus OS cache and per-operation memory; SQLite used 8 MiB private cache per connection. Memory budgets were not equalized.
Pooled PostgreSQL endpoints differ from unpooled SQLite endpoints. PG direct new/reuse/pooled modes expose the connection choice.

Per-row writes prepare once and send one request per row; set variants send one request using JSONB recordsets or an integer key array. Batch JSON is prebuilt for database clocks, inside whole-import clocks.
No PostgreSQL endpoint concurrency, cold-cache, remote-host, sustained-capacity, frontend, crash/power-loss, PITR, HA, production-identity or SQL Server tests.
One-second resource samples cannot attribute individual requests; working sets can double-count shared memory. Agent/tool activity was not isolated or controlled during PostgreSQL passes.
Initial incomplete followup and smoke passes are excluded; historical source snapshots retain the pre-import integer-conversion fix for direct measurements.
